title: From the Moon to the time on your clock
description: Follow sunlight from lunar phases to Earth’s seasons, then separate the motion of Earth from the rules on our clocks.
introduction: Start with something you can notice in the sky: the Moon seems to change shape. Build a picture of sunlight and motion, then use it to understand seasons and the human choices behind civil time.
prerequisites: No astronomy background needed. The last lesson includes simple clock arithmetic.
outcomes: Explain lunar phases without confusing them with eclipses.
Connect seasons to tilt, sunlight angle and daylight.
Distinguish a time zone from its current UTC offset.

lessons.objective: Separate the Moon’s shape from our changing view of its sunlit half.
Compare the hemispheres and explain the effects of Earth’s tilt.
Use fixed offsets while recognising that civil time follows human rules.

glossary.definition: The changing portion of the Moon’s illuminated half visible from Earth.
The inclination of Earth’s rotation axis relative to its orbital plane.
The difference between a local clock and UTC at a particular moment.
